sayings.translation: While it is postponed, life passes by.

sayings.latin: Forsan et haec olim meminisse iuvabit.
sayings.translation: Perhaps one day it will please us to remember even these things.
Resist beginnings; a remedy is prepared too late.
We are not born for ourselves alone.

sayings.latin: Alia in potestate nostra sunt, alia non sunt.
sayings.translation: Some things are within our power; others are not.
sayings.note: Latin rendering; compare the Greek original before approval.

sayings.translation: Withdraw into yourself.
sayings.note: Latin rendering; compare the Greek original before approval.

sayings.latin: Quod tibi fieri non vis, alteri ne feceris.
sayings.translation: What you do not wish for yourself, do not do to another.
sayings.latin_kind: modern Latin rendering from Classical Chinese
sayings.note: Latin rendering; compare the Classical Chinese original before approval.

sayings.latin: Qui alios novit sapiens est; qui se ipsum novit illuminatus est.
sayings.translation: One who knows others is wise; one who knows oneself is enlightened.
sayings.latin_kind: modern Latin rendering from Classical Chinese
sayings.note: Latin rendering; compare the Classical Chinese original before approval.

sayings.latin: Omnia aliena sunt, tempus tantum nostrum est.
sayings.translation: Everything belongs to others; time alone is ours.

sayings.latin: Longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficax per exempla.
sayings.translation: The way through precepts is long; through examples it is short and effective.

sayings.latin: Ignoranti quem portum petat nullus suus ventus est.
sayings.translation: No wind is favorable to one who does not know which harbour to seek.
To live, Lucilius, is to struggle.
We learn not for life, but for school.
sayings.note: The familiar modern reversal is not Seneca's original wording.

sayings.latin: Non est ad astra mollis e terris via.
sayings.translation: There is no easy way from the earth to the stars.
Now is the time to drink.
I have raised a monument more lasting than bronze.
We are dust and shadow.
One who has begun has half the deed done.
Dare to be wise; begin.
Anger is a brief madness.

sayings.latin: Caelum, non animum, mutant qui trans mare currunt.
sayings.translation: Those who cross the sea change their sky, not their state of mind.
There is a proper measure in things.
When I strive to be brief, I become obscure.

sayings.latin: Omne tulit punctum qui miscuit utile dulci.
sayings.translation: One wins every vote who mixes the useful with the pleasant.
As is painting, so is poetry.
Compliance makes friends; truth produces hatred.
Fortune helps the brave.
So many people, so many opinions.

sayings.latin: Nullum est iam dictum quod non dictum sit prius.
sayings.translation: Nothing is now said that has not been said before.
I fear the Greeks even when they bring gifts.
From one, learn about them all.

sayings.latin: Una salus victis nullam sperare salutem.
sayings.translation: The one safety for the defeated is to hope for no safety.
They can because they believe they can.
The descent to Avernus is easy.
Mind moves matter.
Fortune favors the daring.
Each person is drawn by their own pleasure.
Relentless work conquered all.
Irrecoverable time is fleeing.

sayings.latin: Fas est et ab hoste doceri.
sayings.translation: It is right to learn even from an enemy.
I see and approve the better course, but follow the worse.
Time, the devourer of things.
A drop hollows out a stone.
The strictest law can become the greatest injustice.
For laws fall silent amid arms.

sayings.latin: Legum servi sumus ut liberi esse possimus.
sayings.translation: We are servants of the laws so that we may be free.
Let the welfare of the people be the highest law.
Oh, the times! Oh, the customs!

sayings.latin: Nescire quid ante quam natus sis acciderit, id est semper esse puerum.
sayings.translation: Not to know what happened before you were born is always to remain a child.

sayings.latin: Amicus certus in re incerta cernitur.
sayings.translation: A sure friend is recognized in uncertain circumstances.
sayings.attribution: Ennius, fragment quoted by Cicero, De Amicitia 64
sayings.source_title: Ennius, fragment quoted by Cicero, De Amicitia 64

sayings.latin: Concordia parvae res crescunt, discordia maximae dilabuntur.
sayings.translation: Through harmony small things grow; through discord the greatest collapse.
Without anger or partiality.
The more corrupt the state, the more numerous the laws.
Everything unknown is taken as magnificent.
Where they make a desert, they call it peace.

sayings.latin: Non est vivere, sed valere vita est.
sayings.translation: Life is not merely being alive, but being well.
No day without a line.
sayings.attribution: Traditional Latin rendering of Pliny, Naturalis Historia 35.84
sayings.source_title: Traditional Latin rendering of Pliny, Naturalis Historia 35.84
sayings.note: Pliny recounts the saying in relation to the painter Apelles.

sayings.lead: Radio waves, visible light, and X-rays are all electromagnetic radiation.
sayings.body: They differ in wavelength, frequency, and energy, but all belong to the same spectrum.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: The Rosetta Stone carries one decree in three writing systems.
sayings.body: Its Greek, Demotic, and hieroglyphic texts became central to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs.
sayings.attribution: The British Museum, The Rosetta Stone
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: A GPS satellite clock would run about 38 microseconds per day faster than a clock on Earth without correction.
sayings.body: Special relativity slows it by about 7 microseconds per day, while weaker gravity speeds it by about 45.
sayings.attribution: NIST, Putting Einstein to the Test
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: LIGO's first gravitational-wave signal changed the length of a four-kilometre detector arm by roughly one-thousandth of a proton's diameter.
sayings.body: Laser interferometry measured that minute distortion as two black holes merged more than a billion light-years away.
sayings.attribution: LIGO Laboratory, The First Detection of Gravitational Waves
sayings.source_title: The First Detection of Gravitational Waves
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: One SI second corresponds to exactly 9,192,631,770 periods of radiation from a specified caesium-133 transition.
sayings.body: The definition fixes a microscopic frequency rather than relying on Earth's variable rotation.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: The kilogram is defined by assigning the Planck constant an exact numerical value.
sayings.body: Since 2019, the SI definition has not depended on the mass of a particular metal cylinder.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: A clock on the Moon's surface runs about 56 microseconds per Earth day faster than one on Earth.
sayings.body: The difference matters when designing a shared lunar time standard for navigation and communications.
sayings.attribution: NIST, What Time Is It on the Moon?
sayings.source_title: What Time Is It on the Moon?
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: Earth's rotational day is not perfectly constant.
sayings.body: Atmospheric winds, ocean currents, motion in Earth's interior, and the Moon all exchange angular momentum with the planet.
sayings.attribution: NIST, What Determines the Length of the Day?
sayings.source_title: What Determines the Length of the Day?
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: Quantum fluctuations can move each of LIGO's 40-kilogram mirrors by about 10^-20 metre.
sayings.body: The detector uses squeezed quantum states of light to reduce this measurement noise.
sayings.source_title: Quantum Squeezing Lets Gravity-Wave Detectors See More
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: The modern SI is built from seven defining constants whose numerical values are exact.
sayings.body: Those constants include the speed of light, Planck constant, elementary charge, and caesium hyperfine frequency.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: A clay tablet from about 1750 BCE records Nanni's complaint to the merchant Ea-nasir about poor-quality copper.
sayings.body: The letter also objects to delays and the treatment of Nanni's messenger.
sayings.source_title: Clay tablet: letter from Nanni to Ea-nasir
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: The Pony Express operated for only eighteen months, from April 1860 to October 1861.
sayings.body: Its relay system could carry mail more than 1,800 miles in about ten days.
sayings.attribution: U.S. National Park Service, Pony Express National Historic Trail
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: A voice recorded on paper in 1860 became recoverable audio only in 2008.
sayings.body: Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville's phonautograph traced sound waves but was not designed to play them back.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: British cryptographers deciphered the Zimmermann Telegram before the United States entered the First World War.
sayings.body: The message proposed a German-Mexican alliance and offered Mexico territory in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: By 1915, six U.S. cities had more than fifty-six miles of pneumatic tubes carrying mail beneath their streets.
sayings.body: Compressed air propelled sealed canisters between main and branch post offices.
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: John Harrison's H4 marine timekeeper ticks five times each second.
sayings.body: During its 1761 trial voyage, Harrison's son used it to predict an earlier landfall at Madeira than the ship's crew expected.
sayings.source_title: Longitude found: the story of Harrison's timekeepers
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: Herman Hollerith's punched-card tabulator sensed holes using pins, mercury cups, and electrical circuits.
sayings.body: The system helped complete the 1890 U.S. census tabulation in one year after the 1880 census had taken eight.
sayings.attribution: Library of Congress, Hollerith's Electric Sorting and Tabulating Machine
sayings.source_title: Plate, punch card, and instructions for Herman Hollerith's Electric Sorting and Tabulating Machine
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.lead: When North American railroads adopted standard time in 1883, some communities briefly experienced two versions of noon.
sayings.body: One was local solar noon; the other was noon under the new railway time zone.
sayings.attribution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Synchronizing Time
sayings.note: Verify the wording and linked source before approval.

sayings.translation: All things flow.
sayings.latin_kind: modern Latin rendering from Ancient Greek

sayings.latin: Non est via regia ad geometriam.
sayings.translation: There is no royal road to geometry.
sayings.attribution: Euclid, reported by Proclus in his Commentary on Euclid's Elements
sayings.source_title: Euclid, reported by Proclus in his Commentary on Euclid's Elements
sayings.source_text: μὴ εἶναι βασιλικὴν ἀτραπὸν ἐπὶ γεωμετρίαν
